diagnosis: I calibrated HBV on the whole 1971–1997 record (with 1970–71 as warm-up) and got daily NSE 0.817 (KGE 0.83, r 0.91). The model overestimates total flow by about 9%. I first tested how well a calibration transfers between periods. Parameters calibrated on 1971–84 gave NSE 0.83 there and 0.77 on 1984–97. Calibrating on 1984–97 alone reached only about 0.81 and still overestimated flow by about 13%. So the model consistently produces too much water in the later years, which suggests the forcing or the catchment's water balance changed over time. The submitted set comes from a better optimum found on the full record by restarting from the late-period parameters. Its main values are a large soil store (FC about 410 mm, LP 0.9) with a strongly non-linear runoff response (BETA about 7). Flow is mainly quick and medium-speed (K0 0.29, K1 0.20, UZL about 6) with a slow groundwater store (K2 0.027) and short routing (MAXBAS about 2.7). Precipitation is scaled down through the snowfall correction (SFCF 0.84). Snow matters very little here. Weak points: total volume and low flows in dry years, and some flood peaks timed or sized wrongly. Calibration runs from different starting points disagreed on the fast-flow parameters (K0, UZL), so those are uncertain. I am more confident in the soil parameters, which stayed similar across runs. I expect NSE of about 0.75–0.80 in 1998–2008.
